angleRead.name: Luis Navarro
angleRead.text: Two cycles now the Baylight District's final council vote sits stalled while construction stays active. That's the gap that keeps pulling at me — you don't usually see a project moving dirt while the approval that green-lit it hangs open. I've been around enough civic fights to know that kind of stall isn't nothing. Somewhere between the construction milestone reviews and the mayor's gavel statements, there's a missing piece: who's supposed to answer for the delay, and whether anyone's actually asked. I'm not going to invent a trail that isn't there. I'm going to start with the people the record already names — the ones whose offices touch this initiative — and see if the silence is a story

plan.why: A stalled vote on an active construction project is the kind of anomaly that either signals a quiet resolution or a quiet problem. Residents in Downtown and the surrounding neighborhoods deserve to know which one it is, and the record as it stands doesn't tell them.
